title: Gronin playbook
description: The shape of a playbook. This schema is the shape layer only: it is published so editors can complete and lint a playbook, and it is NOT the gate. The semantic refusals - path traversal resolution, MCP server existence, shell detection in a tool set, the receipt check - cannot be expressed here and live in the runtime's validator. A playbook that satisfies this schema may still be refused at load, by design. Interpolation is namespaced (${config.x} or ${trigger.x}); the shape layer does not check that either, so a bare ${x} passes here and is refused by the runtime (FR-039).

description.description: Required by the runtime when agent.restricted is false: turning off the coarsest bound is a decision and has to be stated.

schedule.description: Required when type is cron. Standard five-field cron expression.

restricted.description: Removes the command- and code-running built-in tools at the process level. Default true.

tools.description: The replacing tool set. The runtime refuses a shell or a writing tool here; the schema cannot tell them apart.

mcp.description: Server names. The runtime refuses a name this deployment does not provide.

allow.description: Path-scoped file tools and individually named MCP tools. The runtime refuses an entry naming a whole server, and resolves every path before deciding.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema the agent report is validated against. An object, because that is what the runtime compiles: a string was accepted here and named a schema file the runtime never resolved, so it passed the load gate and failed every run after the agent had been paid for.

items.description: One key naming the sink type, whose value configures it. The runtime refuses a type this deployment does not implement (FR-038) and a creating sink without a cap; neither is knowable from the shape alone.

guard.description: Shape only: the durations of the claim set belong to the deployment and are checked by the runtime at startup, not here. An unknown key is refused (FR-119), and so is a key this runtime does not apply yet, by the load gate rather than by this schema.

runs.description: At most this many runs start within any window of `per` (FR-114). A run counts from the moment it starts, whatever its outcome.

per.description: The window, in whole minutes or hours. Keyed on the playbook name alone.

rate.description: A trigger this refuses is discarded, never made to wait (FR-116).

wait.description: How long a trigger refused because the playbook is already running may wait for it (FR-112). A zero duration still enters the waiting slot and expires at once, recorded as wait_expired.

retrieve.description: Reserved. The runtime refuses a playbook declaring this block rather than accepting and ignoring it: a declared bound that nothing applies is worse than an absent one.
